shared_contract_decision_supersession_re: The approved shared-pip-distribution model made every plugin's pyproject.toml depend on an unpublished sibling distribution (knowledge-workbench-contracts), which conflicts with this repository's plugin-independence rule (.agent/rules/plugin-architecture-policy.md) and cannot actually be proven standalone-installable. Corrected model: each producer plugin materializes its own contract schema/validator inside its own package; consumers carry generated, hash-checked copies rather than a shared pip dependency. See the correction doc for the full model and the new Plugin Self-Containment Gate.

atomic_output_disposition.superseded_note: The shared knowledge-workbench-runtime distribution is no longer a valid disposition for the same standalone-installability reason as the contracts distribution. Wave 4/5 must materialize create_staging_dir/promote inside each of canonical-knowledge and knowledge-publication directly, not import a shared runtime package. Zero plugins consume this distribution as of the correction, so no code rollback was needed -- this is a forward-looking correction for Waves 4/5.

convert_py_extraction_primitive_unificat.note: run_pandoc_extraction (convert.py) and _run_pandoc_raw (analyze_structure.py, now source-document-extraction-owned) are structurally parallel direct-pandoc-invocation functions; whether they become one shared source-document-extraction primitive or remain two is a Wave 2 implementation decision, not resolved here.

orchestrate_conversion_retention_note: Not retired in Wave 6, unlike the original plan's proposal. Preserves the analyze -> human confirmation -> canonical construction -> render sequence as the intentional public workflow orchestrator. Must contain orchestration only, no domain logic. All four skill dispositions (including this one) are reassessed in Wave 7 using the final consumer scan; this approval does not pre-approve retirement of any of the four.

approval.note: Approved with three revisions to the original proposal: (1) a more extraction-favoring analyze_structure.py split, (2) a new separate knowledge-workbench-runtime distribution instead of duplicating or promoting atomic_output.py into contracts, (3) orchestrate-conversion retained rather than retired, with all four skill dispositions reassessed in Wave 7 using real consumer evidence, not pre-approved for removal.
